message.reasoning_content:
I am reviewing the VP's draft payment decision to identify errors.

I will object only to concrete problems: ignored findings, unsupported reasons, or approval despite a reject-severity finding or high risk.

I am checking the draft against specific criteria. A rejection needs a reject-severity finding or high risk memo; doubts nobody can verify are not enough. Over $10,000 requires explicit resolution of every finding and risk signal. I will name exact finding IDs or claims in any objection. The vendor master record is from our own systems. I will not object to style.

The invoice math checks out. The subtotal is $9,500. Tax is 5%. The due date is correct. The risk memo is low with no signals. F1 and F2 are both benign information findings.

The vendor master confirms the alias match. The draft addresses every finding and risk signal. No concrete error remains.

The draft's reliance on the vendor master and risk memo is valid. The vendor name spelling matches the master record. The empty earlier_invoices field is acceptable. I am now checking whether the note to contact Jim at ext 4421 with questions constitutes instructions to the reviewer.

The note to contact Jim at ext 4421 is a contact detail, not an instruction to the payment reviewer. The risk memo already confirms no instructions beyond automated findings appear on the invoice.

The draft is sound. No concrete error remains.
